name: qiu-sld-campus-hub
title: QIU SLD Campus Hub
description: Club hub plus digital Student Life Division forms and approvals
readmeHtml:
QIU SLD Campus Hub

The Student Life Division portal for Quest International University (QIU), Ipoh.

An Instagram-style home for clubs and student life, plus a back office that turns every official SLD template into a web form, routes it through digital approval chains, and prints it back in the exact official layout.

Live demo →

Core principle: nobody types a fact the system already knows. Identity, programme, year group, positions, club and event details come from university records and are locked.

How it works

An event, from idea to archive

flowchart LR
    A[Committee drafts proposal<br/>live, autosaved] --> B[Preparer signs]
    B --> C[Advisor signs]
    C --> D{SLD}
    D -- needs Dean / COO / Registrar --> P[Export · sign on paper<br/>upload scan · tick signers]
    P --> E
    D -- approves --> E[Approved 🎉]
    D -- marks parts --> R[Returned to fix] --> B
    E --> F[Posted to the feed<br/>followers notified]
    E --> G[Registration · tickets · QR attendance]
    G --> H[Completion package<br/>photos · post mortem · finance]
    H --> I[SLD tracker]

A late proposal (under the 14-day lead time) or a budget deficit needs a written reason, and SLD must approve it explicitly. That decision is recorded with the signature.

A club's year

flowchart LR
    N[New club application<br/>President → Advisor → SLD] --> O[Club opens with<br/>committee and advisor]
    O --> W[Weekly activities<br/>minutes + 3 photos]
    O --> EV[Events]
    W & EV --> Y[AGM: year in review<br/>report · election · package]
    Y --> K[SLD acknowledges<br/>archive ZIP built]
    K --> HO[SLD starts handover<br/>new committee: view-only training]
    HO --> T[Overlap ends: new committee in charge<br/>old committee thanked + certificates]

Money

flowchart LR
    M[Membership payment<br/>receipt checked once across all clubs] --> L[(Club ledger)]
    WD[Fund withdrawal<br/>Treasurer → President → Advisor → SLD] --> FI[Finance transfers<br/>within 14 days, else flagged]
    FI --> BI[Treasurer uploads bank-in] --> SC[SLD confirms] --> L
    PU[Event purchases<br/>receipt read by AI] --> L

Architecture

flowchart TB
    subgraph Browser
        V[React 19 + Inertia · TypeScript<br/>installable PWA]
    end
    subgraph Laravel
        C[Thin controllers + form requests] --> S[Services: business rules]
        C --> PO[Policies: every permission server-side]
        S --> Q[Queued jobs: AI drafting, archives, PDFs]
    end
    V <--> C
    S --> DB[(MySQL / SQLite)]
    S --> CS[(camsys: read-only<br/>student records)]
    S --> ST[Private storage<br/>signed, expiring links]
    Q --> AI[Claude: drafting, receipts, assistant]
    Q --> LO[LibreOffice · PhpWord · python-pptx<br/>official template output]
    C --> G[Google: sign-in, Calendar, Meet]

Features

Social (students)

  • Club profiles with logo, category, bio, Instagram, permanent club QR
  • Committee tab with session selector: photo, position, course short form, year group; tap for profile card
  • Lifelong student profile with a personal permanent QR (portfolio fields only)
  • News feed: last 7 days in full, older posts folded into 8–14 days, months and years; followers notified of new posts and events; likes and comments (who liked, who commented) notify the committee
  • Feed hygiene: bad-word and insult filter (English, Malay, Manglish, leet/spaced spellings), per-club and per-event posting limits, no repeat captions or comment floods
  • Committee year timeline on the club page

Portal (committees, advisors, SLD)

  • Google sign-in restricted to @qiu.edu.my. A camsys student or registered staff member is linked to their record on first sign-in (never duplicated). Any other QIU account becomes a limited student with no student record: it cannot hold a committee position until camsys has it, and the nightly sync then links it to the same account. Staff and admin roles are never created automatically
  • Nightly camsys sync (read-only) with automatic year group and academic session rollover (1 July)
  • Scoped roles: club committee and advisor per session; President, Vice President, Secretary and Treasurer compulsory before any submission
  • SLD admin: dashboard, clubs, committees, staff accounts, transfer club to committee, requests to clubs (7-working-day replies), settings, audit log
  • Daily reminders for every deadline (approvals, proposal lead time, indemnity, post-event documents, membership grace, AGM, replies to SLD)
  • Lifelong profile with CCA, positions, verifiable PDF certificates; alumni sign in with a linked personal email
  • Installable PWA (manifest, offline shell); photos re-encoded on upload; private files behind signed, expiring links
  • Event proposals with approval chains and e-signatures, QR attendance, indemnity, posters, post mortem (09)
  • Membership and payments (online receipt check, cash handover), finance ledger (02) and fund withdrawal (07)
  • One receipt pays once: screenshot fingerprint and bank transaction ID checked across every club; sender name checked
  • Transaction IDs CLUB_EVENT|MEMBERSHIPDRIVE-<drive>|NORMALREGISTER_MATRIC_NAME_YYYYMMDD_HHMM_TRANSACTION; SLD finds any transaction by any parts as they type
  • Finance workbook (Excel/PDF): Overview, then membership drive, normal registration, each event, other; this session or all years; pick the sheets
  • Event purchases and claims: snap the receipt (AI reads items and prices), budget vs spending, helpers claim back, event committee verifies, pay back by cash (QR photo) or transfer (name checked)
  • Outdoor events: indemnity pre-filled, sign once registered or paid, ticket appears after signing
  • Meetings with Google Meet, minutes (13) with AI drafting, weekly CCA. Committee meetings invite the committee and advisors only; weekly activities invite the committee or all members, with expected pax and location, and everyone invited is notified
  • Meeting check-in / check-out by rotating QR (like events): only the meeting's audience can check in (committee + advisors, or all members), with times kept per person
  • Meetings report for each club and for SLD (every club), with attendance rate and minutes status, exported to Excel/PDF
  • Each meeting has an Attendance tab (QR, checklist, Excel/PDF export) and a Minutes tab; the minutes go up the approval chain together with the attendance checklist, and everything downloads as one ZIP (SLD can do this for every club)
  • Committees can upload their own check-in and check-out QR images (for events and meetings) and show them full screen
  • All-member activities appear in members' and followers' feeds and calendars, and on the club profile; followers are notified. Committee meetings stay with the committee, advisors and SLD
  • Posts can be reported from the ⋯ menu with a reason; SLD and the Super Admin are notified, as they are when a club submits its membership fee
  • Exports never split a word, date or ID across lines (Excel, Word and PDF)
  • Every notification is also emailed by SMTP (Haraka server in deploy/haraka/, see docs/EMAIL_SMTP.md) in a branded, animated template with a button straight to the action; categories switched off in settings stop by email too
  • Membership grace, termination and alumni managed by the committee or SLD: remind, give more days, end with a reason, mark alumni, undo; members are notified
  • Venue booking (La Place, semester venues, big rooms) with SLD confirmation; daily club status (Active / At risk / Inactive)
  • AGM periods set by SLD, AGM scheduling with Meet link and rotating-QR attendance, AGM Report (01) with AI-drafted objectives/speech/agenda and computed attendance
  • Elections: nominations with full-term check, one vote per position, SLD flags, results into the AGM Report, role handover on 1 July
  • Annual Activities Report (12) as PPTX/PDF from the official template, AI-written event details, SLD themes; AGM package checklist
  • Approval routes per the spec: proposals Preparer → Advisor → SLD (final); withdrawals Treasurer → President → Advisor → SLD, then Finance transfers and the Treasurer uploads the bank-in receipt
  • SLD rules editable in Settings: proposal lead time (14 days), minimum photos (3), Finance transfer deadline (14 days), handover overlap (7 days). A late proposal or a budget deficit needs a reason that SLD explicitly approves, and the approval is recorded
  • Evidence photos required for weekly activity reports, AGMs and finished events. Event photos download as a ZIP named Club_Event_YYYYMMDD_01.jpg
  • After SLD acknowledges the AGM, a yearly archive ZIP is built (AGM, finance, members, annual report, events, weekly reports, photos), visible only to the club and SLD
  • Handover started by SLD after the acknowledged AGM: the incoming committee gets view-only training access during the overlap
  • Event proposal form: live gauge of the compulsory parts; Sign & submit jumps to the first problem (flashes red) and then to each next one (blinks until touched); workshops list speakers (photo required) and need only 2 persons in charge; at least 2 objectives; collaboration with partner clubs or typed-in partners; several trips, each departure → places on the way (last = drop-off) → return, all within the event time; extra headings, paragraphs, bullets, tables and pictures (printed centred, fitted for A4) after the conclusion; unticked ICT prints "Not required"; the export adds a committee chart with student and employee IDs
  • Clubs you run → All events: ongoing, upcoming and past events, with past events by year
  • SLD Proposals & exports: every proposal as PDF or Word, the list as Excel/PDF, and one ZIP per event with all its documents and finance lines
  • My Activities: each club's requests by stage (Draft, Submitted with approval progress, Approved, Rejected); rejected requests clear after 30 days or by hand. Approvers, Treasurers (receipts to check) and the committee (proposal submitted) are notified
  • SLD submissions tracker: weekly reports missing by month, incomplete event completion packages, AGM state, overdue transfers. Finance has monthly and yearly income/expense charts for one club or all clubs
  • One calendar: approved events plus my clubs' meetings, weekly activities, weekly-report due dates and AGMs, with a whole-year view
  • New-club registration: the proposed President applies and signs → the advisor signs → SLD approves. The club, its committee and its advisor only exist after approval
  • Role-aware assistant: answers only from records the person may open, links to them, and keeps a private history the person can delete
  • Report and long forms save drafts automatically (on the server for reports, on the device for new requests); every submission ends with one sign-and-confirm step
  • Higher-authority signatures on paper at SLD's step: choose the signatories, export the official document, upload the signed scan and tick who signed. The final approval opens only when everyone is ticked, and it ends with an approval animation
  • AGM "year in review" compiled automatically for that session only: events with turnout and completion state, weekly activities, money by month and category, and every AGM document
  • When the handover overlap ends, the outgoing committee loses access and each member gets a thank-you and their committee certificate
  • SLD views a club's members and committee fee status (paid, not paid, being checked) inside the admin portal; advisors and committees see the same on the club page
  • Light and dark mode belong to each account, never the device, so a shared phone never shows the previous person's theme
  • Moderation for posts, comments and assistant questions: a word filter that sees through disguises (f_u_c_k, fuc*k, fvck, run-together words) with English, Malay, Manglish and dialect slang, then the toxic-comment model (set HF_TOKEN). Only SLD and the club's committee can delete comments
  • The assistant answers by retrieval from role-scoped facts: fees and approved events for everyone; a club's money, payments and reports only for that club's committee and advisor; everything for SLD. It suggests related follow-up questions and asks when a request is unclear

Tech stack

| Layer | Choice | | --- | --- | | Backend | Laravel 13, PHP 8.4.1+ (64-bit) | | Frontend | React 19 (strict TypeScript) + Inertia.js, Tailwind CSS 4, Vite | | Database | MariaDB / MySQL (production), SQLite (local) | | Auth | Google OAuth (Laravel Socialite), spatie/laravel-permission | | Documents | PhpWord, PhpSpreadsheet, python-pptx, LibreOffice headless | | Tests | Pest |

Backend choice vs the original tech spec. The spec named a Python backend with MySQL. This project uses Laravel (PHP) with MySQL/MariaDB in production and SQLite locally. It covers the same requirements:

  • The same relational database design.
  • The same REST-style endpoints, served through Inertia.
  • Background jobs and a daily scheduler.
  • Python is still used where it is the better tool (python-pptx for the annual report).

Rewriting the backend in Python would change nothing for users and would put the tested behaviour at risk (over 1,600 automated tests), so no rewrite is planned.

Getting started

Requirements: PHP 8.4.1+ (64-bit), Composer, Node 20+, LibreOffice (PDFs), Python 3 with python-pptx (Annual Activities Report: python3 -m venv tools/pptx/.venv && tools/pptx/.venv/bin/pip install python-pptx).

composer install && npm install
cp .env.example .env && php artisan key:generate
touch database/database.sqlite database/camsys.sqlite
php artisan camsys:import-dump          # local camsys copy from the sample dump
php artisan migrate --seed              # roles, lookups, staff, 6 demo clubs
composer run dev                        # or: php artisan serve + npm run dev
  • Local sign-in without Google: open /dev/login-as (registered only when APP_ENV=local).
  • Super Admin: add your email to SUPERADMIN_EMAILS in .env.
  • Google sign-in: create an OAuth client (Web) in Google Cloud, set the redirect URI to ${APP_URL}/auth/google/callback, then fill GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET.

Tests

The automated suite (Pest, about 1,600 feature and unit tests covering roles, payments, signatures, attendance and security boundaries, plus frontend contract tests) is kept in the private development copy and is not published. Before every release: php artisan test --parallel on SQLite and on MySQL, then npm run build (strict tsc --noEmit + Vite).

Database

MySQL schema, tables, keys and an ER diagram: docs/DATABASE.md.

Deploying

  • Exabytes (Plesk): scripts/package-plesk.sh builds qiu-sld-campus-hub-plesk.zip (built frontend, production packages, clean-install SQL, no demo data). Steps: docs/DEPLOY_PLESK.md.
  • Render / any Docker host: the repository Dockerfile (includes LibreOffice and python-pptx).

Starting accounts on a clean install: Super Admin ai@qiu.edu.my; SLD Officer yeeshiu.chong@qiu.edu.my (Admin), who can add and remove other SLD admins under SLD Admin → Roles. Only a Super Admin can grant Super Admin.

Security and privacy

Everything sensitive stays on the server:

  • Secrets (Google client secret, AI keys, DB credentials) live only in .env, read via config(). Only VITE_APP_NAME is exposed to the browser.
  • camsys is read-only: the sync issues SELECT only and copies an allow-list of columns. IC/passport, address, religion, race, CGPA and scores are never read (enforced by tests).
  • Personal data: student phone numbers are encrypted at rest; phone and email are hidden from serialisation; public profiles show portfolio fields only.
  • Authorisation is enforced server-side (policies, form requests, role middleware). The UI never decides access.
  • AI calls run server-side in queued jobs only, with minimal data.
  • Sign-in is rate-limited, every feature has its own limit, and every request has a site-wide ceiling (per person or IP); every role, committee and membership change is written to the audit log.
  • Browser hardening: a strict Content-Security-Policy (scripts only from this site, by nonce), no framing, HSTS, no-sniff, server version hidden; hidden files and scripts in the uploads folder are never served.
  • Demo sign-in (DEMO_LOGIN) is for testing only. On a hosted server it is locked behind a passcode (DEMO_LOGIN_PASSCODE_HASH, a bcrypt hash) and the account list is never sent before it is entered. Keep it off in production.
  • The sample database/camsys/*.sql is dummy data. Never commit real student records.

Roadmap

  • [x] Phase 0: Laravel setup, design system, layouts
  • [x] Phase 1: Sign-in, camsys sync, roles, clubs, profiles
  • [x] Phase 2: Feed, events, proposals, approvals, attendance, indemnity
  • [x] Phase 3: Membership, payments, finance, meetings, minutes, post mortem, venues
  • [x] Phase 4: AGM, elections, Annual Activities Report
  • [x] Phase 5: Dashboards, reminders, hardening, pilot

Guides: SLD admin · Committees · Deploy on Plesk · Database

Project layout

app/Services/            business rules (Camsys, Time, Roles, Profiles, ...)
app/Http/                thin controllers, form requests, middleware
database/camsys/         camsys sample dump (dummy data)
resources/templates/     original/ official SLD templates (never edited), filled/, maps/
resources/js/            Components/ui design system, Layouts, Pages
public/brand/            QIU Student Activity logos and guides
tests/                   Pest unit + feature tests

name: sld-event-verifier
title: SLD Event Verifier
description: Merges attendance and survey data to verify student event participation, fully in the browser
readmeHtml:
🎓 SLD Student Event Verification System

An automated, high-performance web application engineered for the University Student Life Division (SLD) to merge, filter, evaluate, and export student attendance and survey data from Google Meet and Google Forms.

Processes 590+ student records in ~1ms using client-side $O(1)$ Hash Map lookups, saving ~15+ hours per event of manual spreadsheet sorting while guaranteeing 100% PDPA / GDPR student data privacy compliance.

🌐 Live Production Application

  • Live Web Portal: https://sld-event-verifier.web.app
  • GitHub Repository: https://github.com/LeongJinZhou/sld-event-verifier
  • Firebase Console: https://console.firebase.google.com/project/sld-event-verifier/overview

✨ Key Features & Technical Capabilities

  • 🔒 100% Client-Side Privacy (PDPA/GDPR Compliant): All spreadsheet parsing (xlsx SheetJS) and criteria evaluations run entirely within the user's web browser. Student emails, matric IDs, and survey feedback never leave the local machine.
  • ⚡ $O(1)$ Hash Map Data Matching: Cross-references attendance and survey rosters by normalized email addresses in $O(N + M)$ time complexity (~1ms for 1,000+ records).
  • ⏱️ Cumulative Multi-Rejoin Duration Summing: Automatically aggregates meeting durations for students affected by Wi-Fi disconnections (e.g. 10m + 25m = 35m total) so attendees are never unfairly penalized.
  • 🎛️ Customizable Evaluation Criteria Panel:
    • Attendance Duration Threshold: Real-time slider + quick preset pills (15m, 30m, 45m, 60m, 90m).
    • Survey Requirement Toggle: Enforce post-event Google Form submission or evaluate attendance duration only.
    • Star Rating Threshold Filter: Filter qualified students by minimum feedback rating ($\ge 1$ to $\ge 5$ stars).
  • 🔍 Dynamic Column Header Auto-Detection: Resilient header detection algorithm scans spreadsheet rows for keyword aliases (email, mail, duration, time joined, rating, comments), preventing crashes when Google updates template column positions.
  • 📁 Single & Dual File Input Flexibility: Upload JUST Attendance, JUST Survey, or BOTH files combined. System auto-configures rule modes based on uploaded inputs.
  • 🎨 Apple Red & White UI/UX System: Clean, minimal design featuring Crimson Red (#dc2626) accents, San Francisco typography, clear status key legend, and zero-horizontal-overflow responsive CSS for mobile, split-screen, and desktop screens.
  • 📊 Export & Reporting Suite: Custom Excel column selection modal (.xlsx), 1-click email roster clipboard copy, and print-optimized PDF summary report (@media print).

🛠️ System Architecture

flowchart TD
    A[Google Meet Attendance .xlsx] --> C[Dynamic Header & Email Normalizer]
    B[Google Form Survey .xlsx] --> D[Dynamic Header & Email Normalizer]
    
    C --> E[Attendance Hash Map - Cumulative Duration Summing]
    D --> F[Survey Response Hash Map - Rating & Feedback]
    
    E & F --> G[Roster Evaluation Engine - O(1) Lookup]
    
    H[Customizable Criteria Controls: Duration / Survey / Star Rating] --> G
    
    G --> I[Filtered Student Roster]
    
    I --> J[Interactive Data Table & Status Legend]
    I --> K[Custom XLSX Export Engine]
    I --> L[Print-Optimized PDF Summary Report]
    I --> M[1-Click Email Clipboard Exporter]

💻 Tech Stack & Dependencies

| Layer | Technology | Usage | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Frontend Framework | React 19, Vite | Fast SPA rendering & reactive state flow | | Data Processing | SheetJS (xlsx) | Client-side Excel binary reader & writer | | Icons & UI | Lucide React | Modern vector SVG iconography | | Celebrations | Canvas Confetti | Visual feedback upon report exports | | Styling | Modern CSS3 | Apple-style Red & White theme, flexbox/grid layout | | CI/CD & Cloud | GitHub Actions, Firebase Hosting | Automated testing, build, and CDN hosting | | Testing | Node.js | Automated 16-point unit & integration test runner |

🧪 Automated Test Suite

The codebase includes an automated 16-point test suite (testRunner.js) testing 7 core execution groups:

# Run automated test suite
node testRunner.js

Test Coverage Highlights:

  • ✅ Dual File Auto-Merge: Verifies 456 qualified students from sample datasets.
  • ✅ Single File Modes: Verifies attendance-only (481 attendees $\ge 30$m) and survey-only modes.
  • ✅ Multi-Rejoin Session Summing: Consolidates 10m + 25m disconnected sessions into 35m cumulative duration.
  • ✅ Star Rating Filtering: Evaluates rating thresholds ($\ge 4$ and $\ge 5$ stars).
  • ✅ Dynamic Header Locating: Handles uppercase, lowercase, and shuffled column headers.
  • ✅ Exception Resilience: Gracefully handles empty or corrupt spreadsheet files.

🚀 Quick Start Guide

Prerequisites

  • Node.js (v18 or higher)
  • npm (v9 or higher)

Installation & Setup

  1. Clone the repository:

    git clone https://github.com/LeongJinZhou/sld-event-verifier.git
cd sld-event-verifier

  2. Install dependencies:

    npm install

  3. Start local development server:

    npm run dev

    Open http://localhost:3000 in your browser.

  4. Build production assets:

    npm run build

🔄 CI/CD & Firebase Deployment Protocol

The repository includes a GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/deploy.yml). Pushing commits to the main branch automatically triggers test execution, production bundling, and deployment to Firebase Hosting.

Manual Firebase Deployment

# Log in to Firebase CLI
npx -y firebase-tools@latest login

# Deploy to Firebase Hosting
npx -y firebase-tools@latest deploy --only hosting

👤 Author & Lead Developer

Leong Jin Zhou

  • GitHub: @LeongJinZhou
  • Project Repository: https://github.com/LeongJinZhou/sld-event-verifier

This project is open source and available under the MIT License.

name: qiu-cpdc-career-portal
title: QIU CPDC Career Portal
description: Multi-role career and industrial placement platform with AI learning and a gamified XP ledger
readmeHtml:
🎓 QIU CPDC Career Portal & Enterprise Autonomous Governance Platform

Welcome to the canonical source repository for the Quest International University (QIU) Career Professional Development Center (CPDC) Platform. Built with Next.js 15, React 19, Prisma/PostgreSQL, Firebase App Hosting, and an autonomous AI engineering governance engine, this portal connects students, academic leads, industry employers, and alumni into an interactive career development network.

🏛️ Executive Summary & Core Value Proposition

Unlike conventional university career portals that offer static noticeboards, the QIU CPDC Platform is engineered for deep interaction and strict multi-role domain separation:

  • Role-Tailored Workspaces: Every interactive module—from AI Learning & Coursera integration to Workshops, FYP Tracking, and Talent Outreach—adapts dynamically based on the active user's assigned persona and curriculum scope.
  • Append-Only XP Gamification Ledger: Student engagement is tracked through an auditable, append-only ledger (XpEvent). XP points are derived by summing the ledger, eliminating race conditions and ensuring deterministic audit history with strict idempotency keys.
  • Autonomous CI/CD & Security Governance: Every code modification goes through automated quality gates (166 unit tests), pre-push security sanitization (preventing .env, .db, or secret key leakage), and AI-generated descriptive commits prior to GitHub synchronization and Firebase deployment.

🔐 Comprehensive 8-Role Access & Visibility Matrix

The platform implements explicit RBAC and scope-level authorization across eight university personas:

| Role Persona | Primary Scope & Access Rights | Key Module Behaviors | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | 🧑‍🎓 Student | Self-Service / Own Profile (QIU-YYYYMM-NNNNNN). Can read/write personal CVs, diagnostic self-evaluations, and RSVP/check-in to workshops. | • Interactive Study Path & Faculty Roadmaps (Years 1–4)• Coursera integration with deep speaker/syllabus details• Automated QR check-in & consecutive daily login XP streaks | | 🛡️ CPDC Admin / Super Admin | Global Platform Authority. Full read/write access to all university student profiles, role assignment consoles, platform settings, and system audit logs. | • Master student directory with global analytics & override capabilities• Creation & management of high-detail workshops and corporate hiring events• Immutable audit trail verification & outbox idempotency administration | | 🏛️ Faculty Coordinator | Faculty-Wide Scope (e.g., Faculty of Computing). Full visibility into all programmes and students within their assigned faculty. | • Curates faculty-level career paths, milestones, and diagnostic benchmarks• Evaluates faculty engagement analytics and intervenes in lagging student trajectories | | 👨‍🏫 Head of Programme (HOP) | Programme-Scoped Authority (e.g., BSc Computer Science). Direct supervisory control over their specific programme's student records. | • Final approval authority for programme-specific FYP proposals and logbook milestones• Evaluates programme-level settings and reviews student career diagnostic progress | | 📋 Academic Supervisor | Mentee-Scoped Authority. Access restricted strictly to assigned students undergoing internship placement or supervised training. | • Magic-link authenticated supervision without cumbersome credential onboarding• Evaluates weekly industrial logbook entries, verifies host hours, and signs off on milestones | | 🏭 Industrial Training Officer (ITO) | Corporate Placement & Host Management. Coordinates external placement partners and manages industrial training slots across faculties. | • Oversees host partner agreements, placement matching, and supervisor assignments• Tracks enterprise satisfaction and resolves workplace training escalations | | 💼 Employer / Hiring Partner | Anonymized Talent & Recruitment Gateway. Access restricted to verified talent directories; barred from seeing personal student emails or academic probation status. | • Deep talent discovery with automated AI skill-matching algorithms• Direct recruitment outreach via in-platform messaging without compromising PII | | 🎓 Alumni / Industry Mentor | Post-Graduation Community & Mentorship. Transitioned automatically upon internship completion and degree fulfillment. | • Automated transition from active intern to alumni status• Leads workshops, serves as guest industry speakers, and facilitates peer-to-peer mentoring |

🚀 Deep Module Architecture

1. 🤖 AI Suite & Coursera Learning Modules

  • Deep Course Metadata: When students select Coursera or internal training modules, they receive direct enrollment URLs, instructor profiles, prerequisite mapping, and expected XP award totals upon completion.
  • Deterministic Milestone Tracking: Career roadmaps resolve deterministically across all eight faculties and four academic years, guiding students from freshman orientation through capstone completion.

2. 🎟️ Interactive Workshops & QR Attendance Ledger

  • Deep Event Scheduling: Administrators create events featuring speaker credentials, precise timeline breakdown, capacity thresholds, and venue tracking.
  • Time-Gated QR Attendance: QR check-ins open within a strict timing window before and after workshop execution. Duplicate check-ins are intercepted by idempotency validators to ensure XP integrity.

3. 🔬 FYP & Industrial Logbook State Machines

  • Non-Reversible Lifecycle: Final Year Projects (FYP) and Industrial Training logbooks operate on strict state machines (Draft ➔ Review ➔ Approved). Approved milestones cannot be silently transitioned backwards without creating an auditable administrative override.
  • Supervisor Magic Links: External academic supervisors review mentee logbooks via secure, tokenized magic URLs signed with custom crypto secrets (MAGIC_LINK_SECRET).

4. 📈 Next-Best-Action Engine

  • Automatically prioritizes actionable recommendations based on student status (e.g., nudging missing profile details first, guiding upper-year students to submit FYP proposals, and recommending upcoming faculty workshops when baseline metrics are complete).

🤖 Autonomous Deployment & CI/CD Governance Engine

The repository operates under an automated security and deployment pipeline overseen by our governance script (scripts/autonomous_deploy_agent.mjs).

graph TD
    A[Developer / Subagent Code Edit] --> B[npm run deploy]
    B --> C[Step 1: Pre-Push Security Scrub]
    C -->|Intercepts .env / .db / keys| D{Security Passed?}
    D -->|No: Aborts Immediately| E[🚨 Security Leak Prevented]
    D -->|Yes| F[Step 2: Quality Gate Execution]
    F -->|Runs 166 Unit Tests| G{Tests Passed 100%?}
    G -->|No: Aborts Deploy| H[🛑 Regression Intercepted]
    G -->|Yes| I[Step 3: Automated descriptive Commit]
    I --> J[Step 4: Push exclusively to cpdc-platform Root]
    J --> K[Step 5: Firebase App Hosting Rollout]

Mandated Execution Command

Whenever modifications occur, deployments MUST be invoked through the automated entry point:

npm run deploy

This guarantees:

  1. Zero Sensitive Leakage: Automatically scans git staging area and terminates deployment if local .env files, SQLite databases (*.db, *.sqlite), or RSA/PEM keys are detected.
  2. Quality Assurance: Executes all 166 unit tests, requiring a 100% success rate prior to generating commits.
  3. Descriptive Commit Generation: Synthesizes architectural changelog summaries for clear historical auditing.

🛠️ Technology Stack & Cloud Specification

  • Frontend & Server Framework: Next.js 15 (App Router, static & dynamic route pre-rendering), React 19, Tailwind CSS / Custom Vanilla tokens.

name: Pocket-G
title: Pocket-G
description: Secure mobile web client for a remote AI coding CLI over Tailscale
readmeHtml:
Pocket-G: Secure Remote Antigravity Client

Pocket-G is a highly secure, zero-latency, stateless remote web client designed to control a macOS host running the Google Antigravity CLI from a mobile browser. It leverages a direct Tailscale VPN transport layer and runs in an ephemeral, memory-only execution state on the client to eliminate cloud storage risks.

Core Features

  • Stateless Architecture: No database, database logs, or chat histories are stored in the cloud. Client state is maintained strictly in mobile browser ephemeral RAM.
  • Firebase Token Verification: Zero-trust authentication via Google Sign-In on Firebase Auth, verified securely on the Node.js backend using Firebase Admin SDK.
  • Command Blacklist & Path Sandboxing: Keystrokes are buffered and screened against a strict blacklist regex (e.g., preventing unauthorized commands like rm -rf or sudo), and file lookups are sandboxed strictly under the configured ACTIVE_WORKSPACE directory.
  • Mobile-First UX: Sleek, bottom-tabbed UI layout, responsive file system browser, custom xterm.js terminal integration, and an on-screen row of developer shortcut keys.
  • Auto-Kill Daemon: Node.js backend automatically detects WebSocket client disconnections and terminates the underlying pseudo-terminal (node-pty) instantly.

Architecture Overview

graph TD
    Client[Mobile Phone Client] <-->|Tailscale VPN| Backend[Node.js Host Backend]
    Client -->|Firebase Auth JWT| Backend
    Backend -->|node-pty| Antigravity[Antigravity CLI]
    Backend -->|fs Sandboxed| Workspace[Active Workspace]

Security Design

  1. Identity Gatekeeping: Every connection attempts a JWT token exchange. The Node.js Express server validates the token with firebase-admin and enforces that the token email matches the configured AUTHORIZED_EMAIL.
  2. Terminal Keystroke Buffer: Raw keystrokes are intercepted at the backend WebSocket layer. When a command is submitted (indicated by line termination), it is verified against blacklisted command patterns before being piped to node-pty.
  3. Sandbox Enforcement: File reads and listings are validated to ensure paths remain strictly within the ACTIVE_WORKSPACE directory, preventing path traversal attacks.

Setup Instructions

Prerequisites

  • Node.js (v18+)
  • Firebase Account and Project
  • Tailscale client installed and running on both Host (MacBook) and Client (Mobile)

Installation

  1. Clone the repository on your macOS host:

    git clone https://github.com/<your-username>/Pocket-G.git
cd Pocket-G

  2. Configure Backend:

    cd backend
npm install
cp .env.example .env
# Add your Firebase service account details and AUTHORIZED_EMAIL to backend/.env

  3. Configure Frontend:

    cd ../frontend
# Configure Firebase project and hosting settings

  4. Run Backend Server:

    node server.js

📁 Repository Structure

qiu-ims-erp/
├── src/                          # NestJS Backend Modules
│   ├── course/                   # M03: Course, prerequisites, equivalency registers
│   ├── enrolment/                # M07: Add/drop gate & prerequisite impact checks

└── CLAUDE.md                     # Engineering protocols & quick execution guide

🌟 Modules & Key Features

M01: Programme & MQA Repository

  • Curriculum Tracking: Versioned structures governing intakes and cohorts.
  • Accreditation Register: Complete registration of programmes against structural MQA standards.
  • Calendar Types: Supports STANDARD academic calendars and NON_STANDARD calendars (e.g., Medicine, Pharmacy) bypassing automatic credit policies.

M02: Student Academic Profile

  • Active Study Plans: Generates custom semester-by-semester courses according to the student's version.
  • Risk Detection Engine: Automatically flags students whose GPA trajectory or credit withdrawal records show academic distress (PlanStatus: DELAYED / EXTENSION_REQUIRED).

M03: Course & Prerequisite Engine

  • Prerequisite Validation: Strict graph traversal ensuring prerequisite paths are satisfied before enrolment.
  • Equivalency Register: Maps course equivalencies to merge sections across different departments.

M04: Timetable Generator

  • OR-Tools Integration: Bridge connection to Google OR-Tools FastAPI engine.
  • Hard Constraints: No double-bookings for classrooms, lecturers, or student sections. Ensures room capacity validation using combined headcounts.

M05: Venue & Space Manager

  • Interactive Space Allocator: Allocates lecture theaters, labs, and classrooms.
  • Cancellation Recovery: Tracks class cancellations and scores replacement slots by student disruption score, rendering the optimal alternative in real-time.

M06: Exams & Results Module

  • Dual-Obligation Retakes: Automatically tracks fails, plans scheduling inside the student's study plan, and cascades deferred subjects forward.
  • Extension Semester Generator: Automatically appends extension semesters if the standard curriculum duration is exceeded prior to industrial training.

M07: Enrolment & Registration

  • Credit Gates: Strict enforcement of credit caps (20 credits for Long Semesters, 10 credits for Short Semesters).
  • Enrolment Validation: Features interactive "AI Impact Previews" showing downstream prerequisite damage before allowing a subject drop.

M08: HR & Lecturer Management

  • Availability Matrix: Feeds lecturer leave records and preferred hours directly into the solver.
  • Workload Enforcement: Enforces max credit-hour teaching load caps per lecturer contracts.

M09: Finance & Fee Billing

  • Tuition Billing: Auto-calculates fees based on credit hours, course types, and scholarship criteria.
  • Appeal Adjustments: Automatically recalculates adjustments for overloading and retakes.

M10: Notifications & Appeals

  • Transaction Alerts: Push notifications and email dispatches.
  • AI Pre-Assessment: High-fidelity AI analysis of credit overloading (up to 21 credits) and prerequisite waiver appeals using historical GPA trends.

🚀 Getting Started

Prerequisites

  • Node.js: v18.x or higher
  • PostgreSQL: v16.x or higher
  • PackageManager: npm

1. Backend Installation & Database Setup

  1. Clone the repository and navigate to the project directory: 
    cd qiu-ims-erp
  2. Install NestJS backend dependencies: 
    npm install
  3. Set up your database environment variables. Create a .env file in the root directory: 
    DATABASE_URL="postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/uims_erp?schema=public"
  4. Push the schema and apply migrations to your database: 
    npx prisma db push
  5. Seed the database with faculties, programmes, and records: 
    npx prisma db seed

2. Frontend Installation

  1. Move to the frontend directory: 
    cd frontend
  2. Install frontend dependencies: 
    npm install

🛠️ Execution & Verification Commands

Use the following commands (referenced inside CLAUDE.md) to run, build, and test:

Development Commands

  • Start Backend API (Dev Mode): 
    npm run start:dev
  • Start Frontend Dev Server: 
    npm run dev --prefix frontend

Build & Type Verification

  • Validate Database Schema: 
    npx prisma validate
  • Run Backend Compilation: 
    npm run build --prefix . -- --silent
  • Run Frontend Type-Checks: 
    npm run build --prefix frontend -- --silent

Testing Suites

  • Run Backend Unit Tests: 
    npm run test

name: UIMS
title: UIMS
description: University Integrated Management System: AI-augmented monorepo unifying academic operations.
readmeHtml:
UIMS — University Integrated Management System

Overview

The University Integrated Management System (UIMS) is a comprehensive, AI-augmented platform designed to unify academic operations into a single source of truth. By interconnecting every academic stakeholder—students, lecturers, coordinators, HR, Finance, and the Exam Division—UIMS eliminates fragmented legacy portals and automates the most labour-intensive university workflows.

Key Benefits to the University

UIMS is designed not just as a database, but as an operational engine that actively works to improve university administration:

  1. AI-Driven Academic Operations

    • Automated Retake Scheduling: Instantly generates graduation-compliant retake plans for students following exam results, drastically reducing manual coordinator workload.
    • Intelligent Timetabling: A constraint-based AI solver generates conflict-free timetables that optimize room capacities, lecturer availability, and student comfort while enforcing prerequisite rules.

  2. Streamlined Compliance & Accreditation

    • MQA Alignment: Digitizes and enforces approved curriculum structures, ensuring every student's pathway is strictly compliant.
    • Automated Reporting: Pulls real-time pass rates, completion timelines, and delivery data directly into accreditation templates.

  3. Enhanced Student Experience

    • Zero Timetable Clashes: Guarantees students a seamless registration and class attendance experience.
    • RAG Student Advisor: Provides a 24/7 AI chatbot capable of answering complex, prerequisite-aware academic planning questions.
    • Predictive Support: Flags students demonstrating early academic difficulty via registration patterns to enable proactive advisor intervention.

  4. Resource & Cost Optimization

    • Smart Venue Management: Merges cross-programme equivalent subjects into combined classes to optimize lecturer loads and maximize room utilization.
    • Instant Cancellation Recovery: Suggests the least disruptive replacement slots when a class is cancelled, minimizing downtime.

System Architecture

UIMS is built using a modern, scalable monorepo architecture:

  • Frontend (Web): React 18, Vite, Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/ui.
  • Frontend (Mobile): React Native (Expo) for cross-platform access.
  • Backend (API): Node.js 20 LTS, NestJS (REST + GraphQL hybrid), Bull queues.
  • Timetable Engine: Python (FastAPI) wrapping the Google OR-Tools constraint solver.
  • Database Layer: PostgreSQL 16 with Prisma ORM, Redis for caching, and pgvector for AI embeddings.

Getting Started (Development)

Prerequisites

  • Node.js (v20+)
  • pnpm (v9+)
  • Docker Desktop
  • Python 3.12+

Installation

  1. Install dependencies:

    pnpm install

  2. Start external services (PostgreSQL, Redis) via Docker:

    pnpm docker:up

  3. Setup Database:

    cp .env.example .env
pnpm db:push
pnpm db:seed

  4. Run the Development Servers:

    pnpm dev

    The Web app will be available at http://localhost:5173 and the API at http://localhost:3000.

This project is proprietary and confidential. Unauthorized copying, distribution, or use is strictly prohibited.

name: OCR1
title: Medical Report OCR
description: Digitises medical reports from photos and PDFs
readmeHtml:
Medical Report Digitization App

Overview

This project is a cross-platform application built using Flutter that allows users to digitize medical health reports. Users can either capture images of reports or upload PDF documents. The app extracts structured medical data using OCR and stores it in a cloud-based database.

Features

  • Capture medical reports via camera
  • Upload PDF documents
  • Optical Character Recognition (OCR)
  • Structured data extraction
  • Cloud storage integration with BigQuery
  • User verification and editing of extracted data

Architecture

The system follows a client-server architecture:

Frontend (Flutter App)

  • Handles UI and user interaction
  • Captures images and uploads PDFs
  • Sends data to backend

Backend

  • Processes files using OCR
  • Extracts structured data
  • Sends processed data to BigQuery

Database

  • Google BigQuery for storing structured medical data

Installation

Prerequisites

  • Flutter SDK installed
  • Node.js or Python backend environment
  • Google Cloud account

Steps

  1. Clone the repository
  2. Install dependencies: flutter pub get
  3. Run the app: flutter run

Backend Setup

  1. Set up Google Cloud project
  2. Enable Vision API and BigQuery
  3. Configure service account credentials
  4. Deploy backend API

Usage

  1. Open the app
  2. Upload or capture a medical report
  3. Wait for OCR processing
  4. Review extracted data
  5. Submit to cloud storage

Future Enhancements

  • AI-based medical insights
  • Integration with personal health dashboards
  • Multi-language OCR support
